Q: Ruby On Rails 4.2 End Of Life A:

UPDATE: Rails 8.0 and lower are no longer in active support as of May 7, 2026. Security support for 7.2 and 8.0 expires in Aug and Nov, respectively.

UPDATE: Rails 6.0.0 was released on August 15, 2019: https://weblog.rubyonrails.org/2019/8/15/Rails-6-0-final-release/

This marks the official end of support for Rails 4.

The end is nigh! Rails 6.0.0.rc1 was released April 24, 2019. (And now, Rails 6.0.0.rc2 on July 30.) When 6.0.0 final is released in ”a few weeks", that will indicate the end of life for Rails 4 support.

Expect that in September 2019. (I'll update this answer when it ships,) Watch for updates on https://weblog.rubyonrails.org/releases/

If you have not started updating your existing Rails 4 applications to Rails 5, it's time to get on it. The good news is, this major version upgrade looks more straightforward than previous major version upgrades.

Here is a brief overview: https://www.ombulabs.com/blog/rails/upgrades/upgrade-rails-from-4-2-to-5-0.html

Here is the official upgrade document, with more detail: https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-4-2-to-rails-5-0

Q: `NULL` and non-result-set values both return `NULL` when using IN subquery in Apache IoTDB SELECT clause A:

Similar to the answer here, convert a NULL result to false.

SELECT product_id, price, 
       COALESCE(price IN (
            SELECT price 
            FROM products 
            WHERE category = 'A', false)) AS is_in_category 
FROM products;

Q: How to unit test RelayCommand that Executes an async method? A:

first and foremost better to use AsyncRelayCommand from e.g. CommunityToolkit.MVVM framework

By relaying logic to the ViewModel via delegates, it keeps your View purely focused on the UI and your ViewModel purely focused on logic.

to be sure to make pure decoupling that will ease testing. But several recommendations (by google & msdn) should better to follow as well:

Advanced Testing Techniques

  • Testing Asynchronous Commands: For AsyncRelayCommand, you often need to await the execution task or verify the IsRunning property to ensure the task started correctly.
  • Mocking Dependencies: If your command calls a service (like an API or database), use a mocking framework like Moq to verify the service was called without actually making a network request.
  • Monitoring CanExecuteChanged: You can subscribe to the event in your "Arrange" phase and set a flag to "true" to verify the command notified the UI of a change.

Best Practices

  • Keep Commands Thin: Commands should ideally just call a method in your ViewModel. This makes the logic easier to test independently of the command object itself.
  • Follow AAA Pattern: Structure tests using Arrange (set up objects), Act (call the command), and Assert (verify results).
  • Test Parameters: If your command uses RelayCommand, ensure you pass a valid parameter of type T to the Execute method during tests.

Q: Microsoft.OpenApi.Models Namespace Not Found Even After Installing Swagger/OpenAPI Package A:

Migration Overview

Migrating to Swashbuckle.AspNetCore v10+ will likely involve changes in the following areas:

  • Update any NuGet package references for Swashbuckle.AspNetCore and Microsoft.OpenApi to v10.0.0+ and v2.3.0+ respectively.

  • Update any using directives that reference types from the Microsoft.OpenApi.Models namespace to use the new namespace Microsoft.OpenApi.

If you're using .Net 10, checkout the Migration overview to properly setup OpenAPI/Swagger: https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/blob/HEAD/docs/migrating-to-v10.md#migration-overview
